app.name: RAGView
app.headline: Ask a question. {watch} a RAG system answer it.
app.lede: Every number, line and highlight below comes from a real pipeline run on {docs} Wikipedia articles about space exploration: real chunking, real embeddings, real vector search. Only the final answer is simulated.

ask.replayHint: This run was recorded at build time and replays instantly. Ask your own question to run the pipeline live in your browser.
ask.liveHint: Embedding, search and reranking just ran on this device. Nothing was sent to a server.

models.once: One-time download, cached by your browser.

status.building: Embedding {done} of {total} chunks in your browser · about {eta} s left

params.title: Pipeline settings
params.customNotice: No precomputed index for these settings: the whole corpus ({n} chunks) will be chunked and embedded on this device. Expect up to a minute on a laptop; it is cached afterwards.
params.rerankDownload: Downloads a {size} model on first use.

chunking.title: Chunking
chunking.body: A retriever can't hand a whole article to the model, so every document is cut into chunks of at most {size} tokens. Neighbouring chunks share up to {overlap} tokens of overlap so a fact sitting on a boundary still lives whole in one of them.
chunking.notice: Drag the sliders: the chunks below are recomputed instantly with the same tokenizer the model uses.

embedding.title: Embedding
embedding.body: An embedding model ({model}) reads each chunk and outputs {dim} numbers. Texts with similar meaning get similar vectors, even when they share no words.
embedding.notice: Points appear on the map as their vectors are computed. Position on the map comes only from the vectors; colour is just the article's topic.

indexing.title: Indexing
indexing.kicker: Vectors settle into a searchable space
indexing.body: The {n} vectors are stored in an index. With a corpus this small, comparing the question against every vector (exact search) takes well under a millisecond, so no approximate index is needed.
indexing.notice: The map is a 2D projection (UMAP) of the {dim}-dimensional space. Clusters you see were not given to the model: they emerged from the text.

query.title: Query
query.kicker: The question is embedded the same way
query.body: Your question goes through the same tokenizer and the same model, so it lands in the same space as the chunks.
query.notice: It is placed on the map from its 15 nearest chunks, the way UMAP places new points.

retrieval.title: Retrieval
retrieval.body: The question vector is compared with all {n} chunk vectors. The top {k} with similarity of at least {threshold} move on.
retrieval.notice: Scores are computed in {dim} dimensions; distances on the 2D map are only approximate. This model rarely scores below 0.35, which is why the threshold sits high.

rerank.title: Reranking
rerank.body: A cross-encoder reads the question and each candidate together and scores how well the passage answers it. It is far more precise than vector similarity, but too slow to run over the whole corpus, so it only reorders the shortlist.
rerank.off: Reranking is off: the {k} best matches from vector search go straight into the prompt.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.kicker: Retrieved chunks are pasted into the prompt
prompt.body: The model never searches anything itself: it only sees this text. The instructions ask it to answer from the numbered sources and to cite them.
prompt.notice: Token counts use the embedding model's tokenizer, a close approximation of an LLM's.

generation.title: Generation
generation.kicker: The answer is written from the sources
generation.body: The answer streams token by token. Each [n] cites a source from the prompt: hover it to see the passage on the map and the exact evidence.
generation.notice: Simulated: no LLM runs in this demo. Curated questions use a hand-written answer whose sentences are only stated if their evidence actually reached the prompt; other questions quote the most relevant retrieved sentences.

chunking.apply: Run the pipeline with these settings
chunking.differs: Preview only: the pipeline above ran with {size} / {overlap}.
chunking.legend: Chunks alternate colours; striped text is overlap shared by two chunks.

embedding.precomputed: Precomputed at build time with the same model

indexing.projection: UMAP fitted on {preset}, {neighbors} neighbours, min dist {dist}

retrieval.none: No chunk reached the threshold. The pipeline has nothing to ground an answer on.

generation.missing: Not covered by the retrieved sources: {topics}
generation.illustrative: Illustrative, hand-written: the kind of answer an LLM gives from memory alone.
generation.noRagUnavailable: Comparisons without RAG exist only for the curated questions: this demo never invents an LLM answer.

map.empty: The vector space is empty until chunks are embedded.

failure.title: When retrieval fails
failure.lede: RAG is only as good as what it retrieves. These guided cases break the pipeline on purpose, and the trace shows exactly where.

eval.title: How good is the retrieval?
eval.lede: {n} hand-written questions, each with the article that answers it. A hit means a chunk from that article was retrieved.
eval.note: Measured offline with the same models (uv run ragview eval). Document-level hits favour large chunks; they say nothing about whether the exact evidence fits in the prompt.

about.title: How this works
about.body: Chunking, embedding (bge-small-en-v1.5), vector search, reranking (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) and projection run in your browser through transformers.js, using the exact ONNX files that the Python build pipeline uses. Both engines emit the same typed trace, and tests check they agree. Text from Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0.
